$comment: Every currency and material in Rush Royale, rendered by rushroyale.js on resources.html. Each entry answers the same three questions in the same order, because that is what people actually come to a resources page for. Fields: name, id (becomes the anchor, so other pages can link straight at #magic-dust), kind (the filter facet), summary, facts (ordered [label, text] pairs), tags, detail. Chests were deliberately removed on 2026-08-30: a chest is not a resource you collect, it is the container that hands you one of these depending on its type, and resources.html now says that once in prose instead. No exchange rates, costs or drop rates are recorded here unless they were confirmed from a public source - add them as you verify them in-game. Celestial Shards, Essence and Perk Fragments come from the game's in-game Knowledge Base (recorded 2026-08-27); Rune Keys was confirmed against the in-game description on 2026-08-29, and its former 'season pass' and 'Chest of Magic Dust' specifics were wiki-era guesses that were removed rather than kept. Gems are called Crystals in game, so the entry carries the game's word and its anchor is #crystals. The Laboratory rooms named under Magic Dust and Magic Orbs, and the whole of Bonus Orbs, Star Coins, Pages of Secrets, Faction Cores, Hammers, Bells, Clan Coins, Trading Tokens, Legend Medals, Event Tokens, Lucky Tokens, Heroic Tokens and Dragon Coins, were described from in-game play on 2026-08-30 and carry no flag; where that description gave no source for a material, the entry says so rather than guessing. The experiment odds and the Laboratory's rooms live on resources.html#laboratory rather than being repeated here. The oldest entries are still flagged detail='stub'.

entries.name: Gold
entries.summary: The everyday currency. You will always want more of it, and it is the thing that actually gates how fast your cards level.
facts: The soft currency, sometimes shown as coins. Earned constantly just by playing.
Playing matches, career achievements, quests, watching ads, and chests. Also from Expeditions.
Levelling cards, opening and buying chests, crafting and upgrading equipment, and levelling heroes.

entries.name: Crystals
entries.summary: The premium currency. The game calls them crystals; gems is the community's word for the same thing. You can earn them without paying, just slowly.
facts: The hard currency, named crystals in game. Free to earn, or buyable with real money.
Career achievements, quests, watching adverts, events, and direct purchase.
Chests and shop offers. Spending them on chests is usually better value than spending them to rush timers.

entries.name: Magic Dust
entries.summary: A slow, guaranteed route to a legendary card. It does not expire and there is no cap on how much you can hold, so it is the one resource you can safely just accumulate.
facts: A material you bank up and trade in. The published exchange rate is 1,000 magic dust for one random legendary card.

The Chest of Magic Dust in the Seasonal Items store, which costs a rune key; career achievement rewards; some chests on the season pass reward ladder; and the clan store, at 25 trading tokens for 200 dust.

Nothing but the legendary trade-in, which happens in the Legendary Lab: 1,000 dust for a legendary card. Because it is uncapped and does not expire, there is no reason to rush it — the only decision is when you hit 1,000.

entries.name: Magic Orbs
entries.summary: The reason legendaries level so much slower than everything else. Duplicate cards alone are not enough — every legendary upgrade wants orbs too.
facts: An upgrade material used specifically on legendary units. You need both copies of the card and orbs to push a legendary to the next level, at every level.

The premium track of the season pass, alongside experiment coins, plus events and the store. The Laboratory also makes them: the Magic Lab turns legendary cards into an orb, and the Glutton exchange takes a legendary card for either an orb or another card.

Levelling legendary units — nothing else. Because orbs are the bottleneck rather than the cards, spreading them thinly across many legendaries is usually worse than committing to the two or three you actually play.

entries.name: Bonus Orbs
entries.summary: A magic orb that belongs to one named unit. A bonus orb for Bard takes one magic orb off the price of a Bard level — and you can hold several for the same unit.
facts: A per-unit discount on levelling, counted in orbs: each one reduces the magic orbs that unit's next level needs by one. They go towards unit levels only, and not towards Reincarnation.

Spending ordinary orbs to level an event unit creates them, and they then accumulate on legendary units of the same faction — event units excepted. They also turn up in the Lucky Casket, which is a type of chest.
Levelling the unit they are attached to. They are spent before your ordinary orbs, so a stack of them is a head start on one particular card rather than a free choice.

entries.name: Star Coins
entries.summary: A free level. One coin raises a unit by one level, up to and including 15, with no gold, no card copies and no orbs.
facts: A consumable that buys a single unit level outright, valid up to level 15.
A chance at them among the season pass rewards.

The level you would otherwise be furthest from affording, which usually means a legendary — that is where copies and orbs both bite. One catch: levelling this way creates no bonus orbs, so spending a coin on an event unit forfeits the bonus orb that levelling it normally would have made.

entries.name: Pages of Secrets
entries.summary: One page per season pass, six pages to a book — and the book instantly levels any card you like.
facts: A collectible page. Six of them combine into the Book of Secrets, which instantly levels up a card of your choice.
Completing the free tier of the season pass pays one page. That is the whole supply, so a book is six seasons of work.
Nothing until you hold six. Because the trickle is fixed and unmissable, the only real decision is which card gets the book when it finally lands.

entries.name: Faction Cores
entries.summary: The ascension material, and there is one kind per faction — so ascension draws on five separate supplies rather than one shared pool.
facts: Cores come as Forest, Magic, Tech, Light and Dark. Every ascension a unit takes costs cores.
Ascending units. Ascension matters beyond its own bonuses, because Reincarnation needs a unit at the 4th Ascension as well as at level 15.

entries.name: Celestial Shards
entries.summary: An extremely rare material left where the celestial rifts have been. It is what lets units gain new abilities through Reincarnation.
facts: Fragments that appear where the celestial rifts have been, carrying the power of transforming matter.
The Champion Store, the Clan Store, Dragon Rifts, and unique events of the Isle of Rhandum.
Unlocking new abilities on Reincarnated units. See reincarnation.

entries.name: Hero Fragments
entries.summary: What you need to unlock and level heroes. The steady source is Expeditions, which tick along without you playing matches.
facts: Per-hero material used to unlock a hero and raise its level.
Expeditions are the reliable passive source, and can turn up legendary heroes for gold. Also from chests and events.
Hero levels — which matter more than they look, because every 4th hero level raises your account's critical damage.

entries.name: Essence
entries.summary: What upgrades artifacts. You do not pick which artifact it lands on — the upgrade goes to a random unlocked one.
facts: Not recorded in the in-game text used for this page.
Upgrading a random unlocked artifact. See spells, artifacts & perks.

entries.name: Perk Fragments
entries.summary: Spent alongside gold to develop profile perks, which are permanent bonuses to unit stats or to results in particular modes.
facts: The development material for profile perks.
Not recorded in the in-game text used for this page.
Developing profile perks, together with gold. Perks themselves unlock as the critical damage of your collection grows.

entries.name: Hammers
entries.summary: The equipment material. Nothing at the top of the equipment tree gets built or upgraded without them.
facts: The material required to create and upgrade the most powerful equipment.
Crafting and upgrading equipment. Gold covers the ordinary work; hammers are what the strongest pieces additionally ask for.

entries.name: Experiment Coins
entries.summary: A narrow currency with one use, and it is an unusual one: experiments are the closest the game comes to letting you aim at a particular card instead of hoping a chest gives it to you.
facts: A special-purpose currency, not interchangeable with gold or crystals.
The premium part of the season pass, together with magic orbs, and the Challenge of Hunters event, which pays them down to 20th place.

Experiments in the Laboratory of Experiments, 30 coins each. You nominate five cards you already own — one slot may be a magic orb instead — and each experiment can hand one of those five back: 10%, 20%, 30%, 40%, and the fifth is guaranteed.

entries.name: Rune Keys
entries.summary: What you spend in the seasonal offer store.
facts: A currency spent in the seasonal offer store.
Not recorded in the in-game text used for this page.
Purchases in the seasonal offer store.

entries.name: Bells
entries.summary: The summoning currency. Bells buy the legendary of the week — or, if you would rather, bonus orbs for it.
facts: The currency for Legendary Summoning. A summon gives you the legendary unit of the week; past 500 legendarity you can choose to take a bonus orb for that unit instead.

Summons. A standard summon costs 45 bells and can be repeated as often as you like; the Star of the Week costs 75 and can only be summoned twice. In the last week of a season the summon usually lets you pick the specific card you want, which is when bells are worth most.

entries.name: Clan Coins
entries.summary: What Clan War pays, and the clan store is the only place it goes.

entries.name: Trading Tokens
entries.summary: The other clan store currency, and the one you assemble rather than earn: a completed item collection converts into 25 tokens.
facts: A clan store currency that arrives 25 at a time, in exchange for a completed item collection.
Collection items are given for prize-winning places in Clan War, and clanmates trade them between each other by sending requests in clan chat. Complete the set and it converts to 25 trading tokens.
The clan store: 25 tokens for 200 magic dust, or 100 tokens for a legendary event card. The event card is four completed collections' worth, so it is the long game.

entries.name: Legend Medals
entries.summary: A high-end currency that does not start arriving until you are playing at a high level.
facts: Rewards from 7,000 trophies onwards, or after reaching Division 7. The seasonal quest for taking part in duels pays them too.
Trading for the rewards in the Legend Store.

entries.name: Event Tokens
entries.summary: The regular events' shared currency. It survives the event that paid it, but you cannot hold more than 600.
facts: The currency earned and spent in the regular events — Mirror Match and the Masters' Tournament.

The event stores. Tokens do not expire when an event ends, so carrying them into the next one is fine — but the balance is capped at 600, and anything earned above that is lost, so spend down before a big event rather than after it.

entries.name: Lucky Tokens
entries.summary: A regular event store currency, separate from event tokens.
facts: A currency spent at the regular event store.
Purchases at the regular event store.

entries.name: Heroic Tokens
entries.summary: The Hero Tavern's currency, and the only route to the heroic items in the store.
facts: A currency required to buy the unique heroic items in the store.
Among the rewards of the Hero Tavern event, which is structured like a season pass.
Unique heroic items in the store — there is nothing else they buy.

entries.name: Dragon Coins
entries.summary: One coin from one job: completing the Dragon Outpost during a Dragon Rift.
facts: Completing the Dragon Outpost in the Dragon Rift event.
Exchanged in the primary section of the store.

entries.name: Trophies
entries.summary: Not a currency you spend — a score that decides which arena you play in and therefore what you face.
facts: Your PvP rating. It goes up when you win and down when you lose.
Nothing. It gates arena progression, and new enemies appear as you climb — the Virus boss from arena 7, the Assassin from arena 9. Passing 7,000 also starts paying legend medals.
